New: 1. Body & Physical Sensations
Positive
Somatic Safety (Physical Ease): Feeling comfortable, relaxed, and safe within your own body, without tension or pain.
Physical Vitality (Energy Vigor): Feeling physically energetic, strong, and capable in your everyday activities.
Deep, Calming Breath: The ability to breathe slowly, deeply, and comfortably, bringing a sense of warmth and relaxation to your whole body.
Bodily Awareness (Somatic Connection): Attending to bodily sensations with curiosity and kindness, rather than anxiety or fear.
Negative
Headaches: Frequent head pain driven by tension.
Faintness or dizziness: Feeling lightheaded, unsteady, or like you might pass out.
Pains in heart or chest: Feeling tightness, pressure, or sharp aches in your chest area.
Pains in lower back: Aches, stiffness, or discomfort in the bottom part of your back.
Knots in your stomach (Nausea or upset stomach): A tight, uneasy, or sick feeling in your gut.
Tight or sore muscles: Holding stress in your body, leading to aches, stiffness, or physical pain.
Trouble getting your breath: Feeling short of breath or struggling to breathe deeply or comfortably.
Hot or cold spells: Sudden, uncomfortable waves of feeling very hot (sweating) or very cold (shivering) without a clear physical reason.
Numbness or tingling in parts of your body: A "pins and needles" sensation or loss of feeling in your hands, feet, arms, or legs.
A lump in your throat: A tight, swollen feeling in the throat that makes it feel hard to swallow, even though nothing is actually there.
Feeling weak in parts of your body: Having less physical strength or energy in specific muscles or limbs.
Heavy feelings in your arms or legs: A sensation that your limbs are weighed down, making them feel slow or difficult to move.
Thinking something serious is wrong with your body: Constantly worrying that you have a severe, undetected illness or medical condition.
2. Sleep, Appetite & Energy
Positive
Restorative Sleep: Falling asleep easily and waking up feeling refreshed, rested, and physically recovered.
Balanced Nourishment: Eating mindfully and enjoying food, feeling natural hunger and satisfaction in tune with your body’s needs.
Abundant Energy (Energy to Spare): Having plenty of physical and mental stamina to go about your daily activities with ease.
Circadian Harmony: Feeling awake and alert during the day and naturally tired and ready for sleep at night.
Negative
Poor appetite: Losing interest in food or not feeling hungry, even when you haven't eaten.
Trouble sleeping (Trouble falling asleep): Struggling to fall asleep, waking up constantly, or tossing and turning.
Overeating: Eating much more food than your body needs, often as a way to cope with emotions or stress.
Awakening in the early morning: Waking up hours before you need to and being unable to fall back asleep.
Sleep that is restless or disturbed: Waking up frequently throughout the night or tossing and turning instead of sleeping soundly.
3. Mood, Anxiety & Calmness
Positive
Inner Serenity (Calmness): Feeling peaceful, relaxed, and anchored on the inside, even when things are busy around you.
Nervous System Ease (Regulation): A physical sense of stability and calmness, where your heart rate and breathing feel steady and calm.
Emotional Balance: Experiencing emotions that feel manageable and steady, without extreme, overwhelming swings.
Patient Presence: Feeling content to be where you are right now, without an urgent, anxious rush to get things done.
Negative
Intense mood swings: Emotions that bounce between extreme highs and lows very quickly and intensely.
Nervousness or shakiness inside: Feeling jittery, trembling, or anxious on the inside, even if others can't see it.
Trembling: Involuntary shaking or trembling in your hands, arms, or other parts of your body.
Suddenly scared for no reason: Feeling sudden waves of fear or anxiety without any obvious trigger or cause.
Feeling fearful: Feeling scared, frightened, or anxious about things in general.
Pounding heart (Heart pounding or racing): Feeling your heart racing, pounding, or fluttering in your chest.
Feeling tense or keyed up: Feeling high-strung, on edge, or unable to relax.
Spells of terror or panic: Sudden, overwhelming episodes of extreme fear, dread, or panic.
Feeling so restless you couldn't sit still: Feeling an intense inner urge to move, pace, or fidget constantly.
Feeling pushed to get things done: An urgent, internal pressure to accomplish tasks, leaving you unable to rest.
4. Hope, Outlook & Self-Worth
Positive
Hope and Optimism: Believing that good things will happen and feeling confident and positive about your future.
Self-Compassion: Being kind and understanding to yourself when you make mistakes or face difficulties, rather than blaming yourself.
Meaning and Purpose: Feeling that your life has direction, value, and that what you do matters.
Gratitude and Joy: Feeling appreciation for the positive aspects of your life and experiencing moments of pure happiness or pleasure.
Negative
Feeling chronically empty: A heavy, persistent feeling of numbness, boredom, or a "void" inside that won't go away.
Loss of sexual interest or pleasure: Finding that your sex drive has significantly dropped or that sexual activity is no longer enjoyable.
Feeling low in energy or slowed down: Feeling physically and mentally drained, making tasks take much longer or feel harder.
Urges to hurt yourself (Thoughts of ending your life): Having thoughts of ending your life, or physically hurting yourself (like cutting or hitting) to cope with emotional pain.
Crying easily: Finding yourself tearing up or crying over small things or for no clear reason.
Feeling of being trapped or caught: Feeling stuck in your life, relationships, or circumstances with no way out.
Blaming yourself for things: Constantly taking the blame or feeling responsible for problems that aren't your fault.
Feeling lonely: Feeling isolated, disconnected, or lacking meaningful connection with others.
Feeling blue: Feeling sad, down, or unhappy.
Worrying too much about things: Being unable to stop thinking about potential problems, fears, or future events.
Feeling no interest in things: Losing interest in hobbies, work, or activities you normally enjoy.
Feeling hopeless about the future: Believing that things will never get better and that there is nothing to look forward to.
Thoughts of death or dying: Having thoughts about death, dying, or what it would be like if you weren't here.
Feeling everything is an effort: Even simple, everyday tasks like getting out of bed or brushing your teeth feel like a massive struggle.
Feelings of worthlessness: Feeling like you have no value, don't matter, or have nothing good to offer.
Feelings of guilt: Carrying a heavy sense of shame or regret, feeling like you have done something wrong.
5. Temper, Calm & Communication
Positive
Constructive Communication: Expressing your feelings and needs calmly and assertively, without escalating into fights.
Patience and Calm Reflection: The ability to pause, breathe, and think before responding when you feel irritated or provoked.
Interpersonal Empathy: Seeking to understand where another person is coming from, even when you disagree.
Inner Peace (Non-reactivity): Feeling secure enough in yourself that other people's behavior doesn't easily trigger anger or defensiveness.
Negative
Intense anger: Having a very short fuse, feeling enraged, or frequently using harsh sarcasm and snapping at people.
Acting without thinking: Doing reckless things in the heat of the moment to cope (like binge eating, blowing money, heavy drinking, or lashing out).
Blowing things up: Taking a small disagreement and escalating it into a massive fight.
Arguing in circles: Having the same fights over and over without ever finding a resolution.
Feeling easily annoyed or irritated: Having a short fuse and getting bothered or frustrated by small things.
Temper outbursts that you could not control: Losing your temper and reacting with explosive anger that feels impossible to stop.
Having urges to beat, injure, or harm someone: Feeling a sudden, strong desire to physically hurt another person.
Having urges to break or smash things: Feeling a strong urge to throw, break, or destroy physical objects when angry or frustrated.
Getting into frequent arguments: Finding yourself constantly clashing, bickering, or fighting with others.
Shouting or throwing things: Reacting to anger by raising your voice, yelling, or throwing objects.
6. Relationships & Social Safety
Positive
Secure Connection: Feeling safe, stable, and secure in your relationships, knowing you are valued for who you are.
Interpersonal Warmth: Feeling close to others, enjoying their company, and feeling mutual care and affection.
Social Ease (Confidence): Feeling comfortable, relaxed, and authentic when interacting with or meeting new people.
Deeply Understood: The comforting feeling that the people in your life genuinely listen to you, see you, and care about your experiences.
Negative
Terrified of being left: Feeling desperate to stop someone from leaving you, which can lead to clinging, begging, or constantly needing reassurance.
Rollercoaster relationships: Friendships or romantic relationships filled with constant drama, intense arguments, and frequent breakups.
Feeling critical of others: Constantly focusing on other people's flaws, mistakes, or shortcomings.
Feeling shy or uneasy with the opposite sex: Feeling nervous, awkward, or self-conscious when interacting with people of the opposite sex.
Your feelings being easily hurt: Being highly sensitive to criticism, comments, or the actions of others.
Feeling totally unheard (Feeling others do not understand you): The painful sense that no matter how you explain yourself, other people aren't listening, don't understand you, or don't care.
Feeling that people are unfriendly or dislike you: Believing that others are hostile toward you or don't want you around.
Feeling inferior to others: Feeling like you are not as good, smart, attractive, or successful as the people around you.
Feeling uneasy when people are watching or talking about you: Feeling extremely self-conscious, tense, or uncomfortable in public spaces.
Feeling very self-conscious with others: Feeling intensely awkward or worried about how you appear when socializing.
Feeling uncomfortable about eating or drinking in public: Worrying that others are watching or judging you when you eat or drink in front of them.
7. Trust, Boundaries & Autonomy
Positive
Interpersonal Trust: Feeling safe to trust others and assuming good intentions unless proven otherwise.
Healthy Personal Boundaries: Clearly knowing and respecting your own limits, and communicating them gently but firmly to others.
Respect for Others' Limits: Naturally respecting other people's privacy, personal space, and boundaries without feeling rejected or needing to control them.
Mutual Cooperation: Engaging in equal, balanced relationships where power is shared and both parties respect each other's autonomy.
Negative
Controlling behavior: Trying to micromanage what other people do, who they see, or how they act.
Invading privacy: Snooping through phones, journals, or personal spaces.
Ignoring boundaries: Disrespecting the limits other people have set.
Pushing buttons: Testing people's rules or limits just to see how much you can get away with.
Feeling others are to blame for most of your troubles: Pointing fingers at others rather than looking at your own role in problems (also Being positioned as the aggressor)
Constant suspicion (Feeling that most people cannot be trusted): Finding it incredibly hard to trust people, often assuming they have bad intentions or are out to get you.
Feeling that you are watched or talked about by others: Believing that people are constantly paying attention to you, whispering, or gossip-mongering about you.
Having ideas or beliefs that others do not share: Holding strong, unusual beliefs or viewpoints that the people around you do not agree with.
Others not giving you proper credit for your achievements: Feeling like your hard work, successes, or efforts are ignored or unappreciated by others.
Feeling that people will take advantage of you if you let them: Feeling guardedly protective because you believe others are looking for ways to exploit or use you.
8. Presence, Identity & Grounding
Positive
Grounded Presence (Mindfulness): Feeling fully present in the here-and-now, connected to your body and surroundings.
Clear Self-Identity (Authenticity): Knowing who you are, what you value, and feeling comfortable in your own skin regardless of who you are with.
Cognitive Coherence (Reality Alignment): Feeling that your perception of events is clear, steady, and shared with those around you.
Genuine Intimacy: The ability to share your true self with another person and feel a deep, warm emotional bond in return.
Negative
Not knowing who you are: Feeling like a chameleon with no core personality, or constantly changing your beliefs, goals, and style depending on who you are around.
Twisting the story: Remembering or explaining events in a way that is totally different from how they actually happened.
Shutting down: Completely pulling away from loved ones and hiding your emotions.
The silent treatment: Refusing to talk, answer questions, or engage at all during a conflict.
Thinking someone else can control your thoughts: The frightening belief or feeling that your mind is being manipulated or directed by an outside force.
Hearing voices that other people do not hear: Experiencing auditory hallucinations, like hearing whispers, callings, or voices when alone.
Thinking other people are aware of your private thoughts: Feeling like your inner mind is open and that others can read or perceive what you are thinking.
Having thoughts that are not your own: Feeling like ideas or thoughts have been placed directly into your mind by someone or something else.
Feeling lonely even when you are with people: Feeling isolated and emotionally disconnected even when surrounded by friends, family, or crowds.

Spacing out or feeling unreal (Feeling that familiar things are strange or unreal): Zoning out so intensely that you feel disconnected from your own body, or feeling like the world around you is a dream, strange, or fake.
Having thoughts about sex that bother you a lot: Being distressed or troubled by persistent, unwanted sexual thoughts or fantasies.
The idea that you should be punished for your sins: A strong, distressing feeling that you are bad and deserve to suffer or be punished for your mistakes.
Never feeling close to another person: Feeling a deep, persistent barrier to forming emotional bonds or intimacy with anyone.
The idea that something is wrong with your mind: Worrying or feeling like your mental faculties, sanity, or thinking processes are breaking down.
9. Thoughts, Focus & Clarity
Positive
Cognitive Flexibility (Thinking Clearly): Having a clear, quiet mind that can easily focus on tasks, make decisions, and let go of repetitive thoughts.
Self-Trust and Confidence: Believing in your own judgment and decisions without needing to constantly check, double-check, or seek reassurance.
Mental Stillness: Having a quiet, calm mind free from intrusive thoughts, loops, or persistent worries.
Decisive Flow: Making choices with clarity and ease, then moving forward with confidence.
Negative
Unwanted thoughts, words, or ideas that won't leave your mind: Intrusive thoughts or phrases that keep repeating in your head, even when you try to stop them.
Trouble remembering things: Having difficulty recalling recent events, details, conversations, or tasks.
Worried about sloppiness or carelessness: Feeling anxious that you will make mistakes, do a poor job, or leave things messy.
Feeling blocked in getting things done: Feeling a mental barrier or paralysis that prevents you from starting or completing tasks.
Having to do things very slowly to ensure correctness: Taking an excessively long time on simple tasks to make absolutely sure you don't make any errors.
Having to check and double-check what you do: Feeling compelled to repeatedly verify things (like locks, stoves, or written work) to feel safe or sure.
Difficulty making decisions: Feeling frozen, overwhelmed, or unable to choose between different options.
Your mind going blank: Suddenly losing your train of thought or finding yourself unable to think of anything at all.
Trouble concentrating: Finding it hard to focus your attention on reading, working, listening, or other tasks.
Having to repeat the same actions (such as touching, counting, washing): Feeling a strong urge to perform repetitive physical behaviors or mental rituals to ease anxiety.
10. Comfort Zones & Exploration
Positive
Courage and Exploration: Feeling a sense of curiosity and willingness to try new things, go new places, and face challenges with confidence.
Situational Comfort: Feeling safe, relaxed, and at ease when out in public, in crowds, or traveling on public transportation.
Environmental Mastery: Feeling capable and confident in navigating your physical and social surroundings.
Comfort in Solitude: Feeling safe, peaceful, and content when you are left alone, without feeling anxious or insecure.
Negative
Feeling afraid in open spaces or on the streets: Feeling highly anxious or unsafe in large open areas, public plazas, or out on public roads.
Feeling afraid to go out of your house alone: Feeling terrified of leaving the safety of your home without someone accompanying you.
Feeling afraid to travel on buses, subways, or trains: Feeling panic or intense anxiety when using public transportation.
Having to avoid certain things, places, or activities because they frighten you: Restricting your daily route or activities to steer clear of triggers that cause you fear.
Feeling uneasy in crowds (such as shopping or at a movie): Feeling anxious, trapped, or overwhelmed when surrounded by groups of people.
Feeling nervous when you are left alone: Feeling anxious, insecure, or unsafe when there is no one else around you.
Feeling afraid you will faint in public: Worrying that you will lose consciousness and collapse where others can see you.
